sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Specialty Fresh Bakery Master Franchise and Central Kitchen Ops

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg - Grand Duchy, unitary national jurisdiction, registry seat in Luxembourg City
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg-People's Republic of China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 3 June 1986, entered into force 18 January 1987)

Convention of 12 March 1994 between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with respect to Taxes on Income and Capital, as amended by the Protocol of the same date (in force since 15 July 1995)

Hague Convention of 5 October 1961 Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents (in force for Luxembourg since 1 June 1979 and for the People's Republic of China since 7 November 2023)
EU-China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment signed 30 December 2020, not yet ratified and therefore not presently operative

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, in particular Articles 1 and 710-1 to 710-41 governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies; Law of 2 September 2011 on Business Establishment; Law of 15 June 2018 on Classified Establishments.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), through a Luxembourg notary and the MyGuichet.lu e-filing portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial incorporation deed (acte de constitution) containing the articles of association (statuts), filed with the RCS for registration and publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The minimum share capital of an SARL is EUR 12,000, fully subscribed. For cash contributions, at least 25% of each share must be paid up before signing the notarial deed, and the funds must be deposited on a blocked Luxembourg bank account in the future company's name. Contributions in kind require full payment, a valuation by a réviseur d'entreprises, and are reflected in the notarial deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, THAT: (1) The subscription of the founders to [number] shares of nominal value [X EUR] each, forming a share capital of EUR 12,000, is approved and the paid-up portion is directed to a blocked escrow account; (2) The registered office shall be established at [Registered Office Address], Luxembourg, and may be relocated within Luxembourg by further board resolution; (3) [Name] is appointed manager (gérant) with authority to represent the company; (4) The manager is authorised to open bank accounts, pay registration fees, register with the RCS, apply for the business establishment permit and food authority registrations; (5) All prior actions in furtherance of these resolutions are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Search and Initial Capital Blocking
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) and a Luxembourg commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Reserve the proposed company name with the RCS via the online request or through the notary's pre-check to avoid a distinctiveness and confusion refusal. Open a blocked share capital account in Luxembourg in the name of the future SARL and deposit the statutory paid-up portion. Obtain a bank certificate of payment and blocking addressed to the notary.
required_dossiers: Name reservation request or notarial mandate
Identity documents of all founders
KYC and customer due diligence forms of the bank
Proof of residential address of founders
Bank certificate of capital deposit and blocking
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected on distinctiveness grounds, obtain the written reason, amend the distinctive element and refile. If the bank delays or refuses the blocking certificate, provide an updated beneficial ownership statement or select an alternative eligible bank in Luxembourg.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Articles of Association and Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary verifies the draft articles, legality of the share subscription, capital payment, founders' capacity, and the manager's consent. After confirming all conditions, the founders execute the notarial incorporation deed. The notary arranges tax registration, escrowed capital release instructions, and the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association (statuts)
Bank certificate evidencing the paid-up, blocked share capital
Identity documents of founders and appointed manager
Written acceptance of office by the manager
Certified translations if required by the parties
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a defect in capital payment or consent, remedy by topping up the account or obtaining a certified power of attorney, then reconvene for a fresh notarial appointment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration in the Luxembourg Business Registers and Official Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers, filed through the notary portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary electronically submits the notarial deed, statutory declarations and manager consent to the RCS. The RCS reviews the file, assigns a registration number, and the company obtains legal personality upon registration. The RCS coordinates publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
required_dossiers: Notarial deed of incorporation
Articles of association and legal domicile declaration
Manager's signed consent and, if applicable, sworn undertaking
RCS electronic application certified by the notary
Proof of filing and publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises a query, the notary must reply with the requested clarification within a short regulatory deadline. If registration is refused, obtain a reasoned refusal and challenge it before the competent administrative court within the statutory time limit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Social Security and Statistical Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); Statec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, submit the RCS extract to the AEDT to obtain a VAT number and e-tax filing profile. Register with the ACD for corporate income tax and municipal business tax, enrol with CCSS as an employer, and obtain the statistical identification number. Open the company's active corporate bank account to complete the registration formalities.
required_dossiers: Certified RCS extract
Articles of association and incorporation deed
Identification details of the statutory manager
Beneficial ownership declaration (RBE) confirmation
Description of planned activities and payroll information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any tax or social registration is delayed, use the RCS registration number for follow-up and request a tax clearance certificate from the ACD. Prompt voluntary registration and complete documentation reduces penalty exposure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale PME, Service des autorisations d'établissement (via MyGuichet.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the autorisation d'établissement application through MyGuichet, demonstrating that the bakery chain and central kitchen business satisfies professional qualification and commercial probity requirements. Enclose the RCS extract, evidence of the manager's professional capacity, and a description of the franchise and production set-up. The permit must cover each planned shop and the central kitchen.
required_dossiers: MyGuichet application form
RCS extract and incorporation deed
Criminal record and good conduct certificate of the manager
Proof of professional bakery or food-business management qualification
Description of the central kitchen and franchise operating model
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry requests supplementary information, reply through MyGuichet within the imposed deadline. If the application is refused, lodge an administrative appeal with the Minister and subsequently with the Administrative Tribunal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal, Food Safety and Classified Establishment Operating Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commune (municipality); Administration de la santé – Division de la sécurité alimentaire; Administration de l'environnement; Corps grand-ducal des incendies et de secours (CGDIS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the food business notification and HACCP plan with the health authority, obtain the classified establishment operating permit from the environment administration, and secure fire safety approval from CGDIS before the central kitchen or first bakery begins production. The municipality issues the operating or occupancy certificate for the selected premises.
required_dossiers: Food business notification and HACCP plan
Environmental declaration or permit file for the classified establishment
Fire safety certificate and architectural site plan
Occupancy and construction compliance certificate
Waste, water discharge, ventilation and emissions technical data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an inspection reveals non-conformity, remediate within the provisional notice period and request a technical re-inspection. If a permit refusal is contemplated, correct the submitted drawings and safeguards and file a full administrative appeal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for SMEs and Business Establishment Service, in coordination with the municipal administration and the Administration de l'environnement
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) and operating permit for a classified establishment (autorisation d'exploitation d'établissement classé)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement – Ministry of Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Category 2 declaration or Category 3 notification) under the Law of 15 June 2018 on classified establishments for a bakery and central kitchen; a full environmental impact assessment and Category 1 authorisation is mandatory only if installed production or energy capacity exceeds the thresholds set by the annexes.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater from baking, washing and cleaning must comply with municipal sewer discharge limits for pH, grease, COD/BOD and suspended solids, with greases intercepted before connection. VOC, dust and combustion emissions must meet the limit values of the Luxembourg regulations implementing Directive (EU) 2010/75/EU for respective process sources. Food waste, oils and fats must be collected by authorised carriers and recorded in the site waste register in accordance with the Environmental Protection Agency's waste traceability obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the Corps grand-ducal des incendies et de secours after verification of emergency exits, fire suppression, smoke control and access for rescue services. Occupational health and workplace clearance by the Inspection du travail et des mines confirming ventilation, work equipment safety, thermal stress controls, sanitation and food safety infrastructure of the central kitchen and bakery retail premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes – ACD) for direct taxes; VAT and registration duties: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT). Electronic portal: MyGuichet.lu (guichet.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For resident SARL: obtain business registration number from Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) upon incorporation; the ACD automatically issues the national identification number (numéro d'identification) for corporate tax. For VAT: resident entities apply to AEDT via form 700/710; non-resident entities without establishment but making taxable supplies in Luxembourg must register for VAT on same forms through an appointed Luxembourg tax representative, receiving an LU+8-digit VAT number. Registration is required before any taxable activity commences.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – SARL is fully taxable on worldwide income as a separate legal person, subject to CIT, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax; no pass-through treatment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a check-the-box regime. Elections available: (i) VAT group election (assujetti unique) for closely related persons under Article 60 Luxembourg VAT law; (ii) corporate tax grouping (intégration fiscale) for resident subsidiaries ≥95% owned, allowing consolidation for CIT and municipal business tax; (iii) selective application of anti-hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD; (iv) optional collective investment vehicle treatment for eligible funds.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée – TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 30,000 annual turnover exemption threshold under Article 57 VAT Law for resident small businesses; non-established foreign suppliers have no de minimis threshold and must register from the first euro of taxable supplies made in Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance mandate or digital stamping in Luxembourg. E-invoicing is voluntary in B2B/B2C; mandatory e-invoicing for public procurement via PEPPOL (European standard). The ACD/AEDT accepts electronic invoices but does not operate a centralized clearance API; taxpayers must retain standard audit files (SAF-T) and invoice data for submission upon request.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for (i) goods physically dispatched or transported outside EU customs territory by the supplier or on his behalf within the statutory proof period; (ii) supplies of services directly linked to such export, and certain cross-border services subject to Article 14(2) VAT Law. Claim requires that the recipient is identifiable, the goods leave Luxembourg/EU, and complete documentary evidence is held by the supplier before filing the VAT return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD – Single Administrative Document/DAU)
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill where air freight)
Inward Remittance Certificate (proof of foreign currency receipt/consideration settled through a bank)
CMR transport document or other proof of physical departure
Proof of delivery and fiscal warehouse removal records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT authorities routinely audit export zero-rating; any failure to provide complete export evidence within the legal deadline causes reassessment at standard rate. Penalties include late-payment interest (0.4% per month), administrative fines up to EUR 10,000 per offence, and 10% penalty on undue VAT. In case of fraudulent zero-rating or organized VAT evasion, criminal sanctions (fines up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment) apply, input VAT recovery is clawed back, and joint liability may be imposed on directors or Luxembourg representatives.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), with prudential and anti-money-laundering oversight exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a euro-area member and maintains fully liberalised capital and current-account convertibility under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. There is no exchange-control permit or prior central-bank approval requirement for ordinary capital inflows, profit remittances, dividend distributions, or intercompany loans. The euro is freely convertible; additional foreign-currency accounts in USD, CNH, or other accepted currencies may be maintained at a Luxembourg bank. Mainland CNY is not freely offshore-convertible, but commercial RMB flow can clear through authorised CNH/RMB clearing channels. Restrictions arise only from EU/CFSP sanctions regimes, targeted financial restrictive measures, and CSSF-mandated KYC/AML controls. Profit remittance from a Luxembourg SARL is legally unrestricted, though corporate withholding-tax or substance documentation must be observed under direct tax rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no mandatory surrender, conversion, or holding period for export receipts. Export proceeds may be retained in EUR or foreign currency without limitation. The only statutory obligations are statistical reporting to the BCL within the balance-of-payments framework and compliance with the SARL's ordinary accounting, substance, and corporate-tax filing requirements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BCEE – Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-medium feasibility. A Luxembourg-regulated electronic money institution (EMI) authorised by the CSSF under the Luxembourg law of 21 December 2017 implementing EMD2 may open payment accounts, issue IBANs, and process low-value POS or collection flows. However, an EMI cannot provide statutory capital-escrow attestation, deposit-guarantee protection, or bank-grade correspondent clearing. An offshore digital EMI without a Luxembourg passport is not authorised to hold the SARL's statutory capital or operational treasury balances. Such offshore EMIs should be used at most as a sub-rail for franchisee POS settlement, and only if they operate under a valid EU/EEA passport or an available Luxembourg banking-agency arrangement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, Luxembourg credit institutions require at least one authorised director or an ultimate beneficial owner to undergo an identity interview. Physical presence at a Luxembourg branch or at a notary is commonly required for non-EU UBOs, particularly PRC owners. Remote video onboarding is possible only at the bank's discretion and generally requires biometric identity verification, an existing regulated-bank reference, and complete notarised corporate documents. For a Chinese-owned franchise SARL, the safer and faster route is physical or video-interview verification complemented by apostilled and notarised corporate and shareholder documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: beneficial-ownership opacity caused by multiple PRC shareholders, nominee structures, or an indirect investment holding chain for the Luxembourg SARL.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified organisational documents; RCS excerpt; current UBO register declaration; complete ownership-chain chart with passport copies of all natural-person UBOs; board resolution appointing signatories; notarised and apostilled UBO declaration; source-of-wealth statement; tax-residence certificates; audited or management financial statements for each material shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: sanctions screening or adverse-media hit on a shareholder, counterparty, or Chinese franchisor linked to the bakery chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Individual passport and proof-of-address documentation; completed PEP/sanctions questionnaire; bank-generated sanctions-screening report with no-match determination; negative-news explanation letter; commercial franchise agreement; statutory business licence of the Chinese franchisor; lease evidence for the Luxembourg central kitchen/outlets; bank references from the group's primary Chinese bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: inbound capital remittance lacks a clear economic purpose, contains ambiguous SWIFT narrative, or shows inconsistent transaction values relative to the bakery chain's projected revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital-subscription resolution; capital-payment schedule; share-purchase/subscription agreement; investor's bank statements evidencing legitimate source of funds; business plan and revenue forecast; central-kitchen equipment and raw-material procurement contracts; franchise royalty model; explanation letter cross-referencing each SWIFT payment purpose code and commercial invoice.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for inbound capital from China or other non-EU shareholders: (1) Open a dedicated 'Capital Escrow / Account' at a Luxembourg commercial bank before RCS registration or, for an already-registered SARL, a designated operational account. (2) The Chinese shareholder executes a share-subscription resolution and transfers funds through SWIFT MT103 using the SARL's IBAN and BIC, with field 70/72 containing 'Equity contribution / SARL capital subscription' clearly identifying the underlying contract. If the remitter is a PRC bank, the Chinese bank will apply SAFE remittance-purpose classification and require prior PRC ODI approval and SAFE registration; the Luxembourg bank does not impose an additional Luxembourg exchange-control code, but requires source-of-funds evidence and the bank's own UBO confirmation. (3) The receiving bank performs KYC screening, confirms no sanctioned-party nexus, verifies the remittance against the subscription schedule, and issues the capital attestation required for notarisation and RCS filing. Following registration, funds may be transferred to the operational treasury account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound trade settlements—central-kitchen machinery, raw materials, packaging, and third-country franchise supplies—use SWIFT MT103 for direct cash payment against invoice when the counterparty accepts open account terms. For larger or non-standard import contracts, a commercial documentary letter of credit issued by the Luxembourg bank via SWIFT MT700 is preferred, with subsequent MT707 amendments and MT754 negotiation/acceptance messages. Settlement for EUR-denominated EU supplier invoices uses SEPA Credit Transfer; extra-EUR payments to China or other third countries clear through the Luxembourg bank's correspondent nostro network via SWIFT. All disbursements must be supported by underlying commercial agreements, invoices, packing lists, bills of lading or logistics proof, and recorded in the BCL balance-of-payments reporting where applicable.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards on EUR/USD, EUR/CNH, and other freely traded currencies to hedge verified commercial cash-flow exposure; documentation under ISDA or bank master agreement required.

Non-deliverable FX forwards (NDFs) referencing mainland CNY or otherwise restricted currencies, permitted only when used as a genuine economic hedge for the SARL's China-linked procurement, royalties, or equity flows and transacted with an authorised OECD or Luxembourg-audited counterparty.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (EUR/CNY or EUR/USD) to hedge long-term financing mismatches among bank term debt, Chinese franchise funding, and operating revenues; documented under ISDA/CSA and subject to EMIR reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of shareholders for approval of annual accounts, discharge of directors, and appointment or reappointment of the statutory auditor, if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate governance act; minutes recorded in the statutory minute book and archived at the registered office; no RCS filing required unless the resolution involves a notarized deed or an auditor appointment subject to registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the close of the financial year; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 30 June of the following year; extension only by court order
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct registration penalty for delay, but persistent failure to hold the AGM exposes directors to civil liability, prevents timely adoption and filing of annual accounts, and may lead to ex officio tax assessment and public prosecutor proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing and publication of annual accounts (balance sheet, profit and loss statement, notes, and management report if applicable; abbreviated format permitted for small companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Trade and Companies Register (RCS), published in the Recueil electronique des societes (RESA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the close of the financial year; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal reminder issued by the RCS; on the Public Prosecutor's request, the President of the Tribunal d'arrondissement may order filing within one month under a periodic penalty payment (astreinte) of up to EUR 1,250 per day; directors may incur criminal fines up to EUR 25,000; five consecutive years of non-filing expose the SARL to judicial dissolution or strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the RCS registration file and payment of the annual registration maintenance fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: During the calendar month corresponding to the anniversary of the company's initial RCS registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The RCS file is flagged non-compliant; after reminders, the Luxembourg Business Registers may suspend delivery of official extracts and attestations; persistent default may trigger administrative strike-off procedures and adverse bank and counterparty treatment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmative beneficial ownership declaration in the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: During the calendar month corresponding to the anniversary of the company's initial RBE registration; any change in beneficial ownership or control must be declared within one month after the company becomes aware of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court order may be sought under the Law of 13 January 2019 requiring compliance within a fixed period, backed by a periodic penalty payment (astreinte) of up to EUR 1,250 per day; persistent non-confirmation flags the entity in AML counterparty checks and may lead to withholding of official certificates

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Appointment of an independent statutory auditor (reViseur d'entreprises) and deposit of the appointment document
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCS for deposit; the auditor must be a Luxembourg-approved reViseur d'entreprises registered with the Institut des ReViseurs d'Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Required when the SARL exceeds the legal small-company audit thresholds for two consecutive financial years; appointment is made at the AGM approving the prior year's accounts, and the appointment deed must be filed with the RCS within one month of the decision
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the company fails to appoint an auditor while statutorily obliged, the Public Prosecutor or any interested person may petition the court to make the appointment; directors face personal liability for publication defaults and related fines

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit by a Luxembourg-approved reViseur d'entreprises is compulsory where at least two of the following three criteria are exceeded for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total of EUR 4.4 million, net turnover of EUR 8.8 million, and average workforce of 50 employees. The exemption does not apply where consolidated accounts are mandatory or the SARL belongs to a group meeting consolidated audit thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial registers and annual accounts, as amended; IFRS as endorsed by the EU is mandatory for consolidated accounts of listed entities and may be used for unconsolidated accounts only where permitted; the bakery chain SARL will normally file under LUX GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Law of 13 January 2019, as amended, every SARL must file an annual confirmative UBO declaration with the RBE during the month of the anniversary of its initial RBE registration, even when no ownership change has occurred. Any transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership or effective control must be declared within one month after the company knows of the change. The confirmation is signed electronically by a director or an authorized UBO declarant such as the registered agent, and the RBE data must reconcile with the register of shares (registre des parts sociales). Non-confirmation exposes the company to coercive court orders and AML compliance flagging.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shares / Members (registre des parts sociales)
Minute Book of shareholder meetings and board resolutions (proces-verbaux)
Register of Director and Officer mandates and appointments
Accounting books and supporting records required by the bookkeeping legislation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,800-5,500 per annum for registered office domiciliation and corporate secretarial or registered agent services of a SARL in Luxembourg City
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 9,000-27,000 per audit cycle for a small-to-mid-size operating SARL; proportionally lower for a passive holding entity with clean simplified annual accounts

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (aggregate effective rate for Luxembourg City: 17% corporate income tax, 7% solidarity surcharge on the CIT, and 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Innovation / IP Box: 80% exemption on qualified IP-derived net income, reducing the effective rate to approximately 5% for qualifying IP; participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains; investment tax credit up to 12% for eligible tangible assets; reduced CIT rate of 15% on the first EUR 175,000 of taxable income for qualifying small companies.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_regime_note: Luxembourg LIR Art. 114(2) provides an indefinite loss carryforward for companies; no carryback is permitted. Losses may be offset against future profitable years without time limitation, subject to continuity and anti-abuse conditions.
